summary: Sesame-orange sable cookies: butter, granulated sugar, toasted sesame seeds, whole wheat pastry and all-purpose flours and orange zest formed into two 8-inch logs, chilled at least 3 hours, sliced 1/4 inch and baked 14-16 minutes at 375°F; makes about 48 small cookies.
glance: 15 minutes active, 3 hour rest, 20 minutes baking
3/4 cup toasted, white, black or a mixture
faq: What is a sable cookie?
Sable doughs are a bit like shortbread, but with granulated sugar providing a delightfully sandy texture. They can be flavored with anything from chocolate to matcha tea.
Why whole wheat in a dessert?
The author is generally cautious about whole wheat flour in desserts, using it only where its heartier flavor enhances the other ingredients; with sesame and orange zest it's a natural fit.
How do I toast sesame seeds?
Toast raw seeds in a skillet over medium-low heat, stirring frequently, until lightly browned and fragrant. Don't walk away for long: they can burn and turn bitter in a heartbeat.
How do I shape the dough?

Knead briefly into a cohesive ball, divide in two, roll each into an 8-inch cylinder (rolling firmly if it doesn't stick together), wrap tightly in plastic, roll on the counter a couple of times and refrigerate at least 3 hours or overnight.
How do I serve them?
With tea and a bar of good bittersweet chocolate.

summary: A funny little cheese course: chevre pressed in a 1-inch ring over a salty crust of pulverized rice crackers, mini pretzels, butter, fennel pollen and pepper, topped with a hand-raked strawberry granita; looks like cheesecake but isn't sweet; serves 4 as a cheese course.
glance: 1 cup pureed strawberries, forked every 15 minutes, frozen in about 2 hours
25 g rice crackers, 10 g mini pretzels, 25 g butter, fennel pollen, pepper
faq: What is the idea behind this dish?

Pure play: a cheese course that looks like cheesecake but isn't particularly sweet. A cheese course, like an amuse bouche or tapa, is a chance to be less constrained, using bold flavors and surprising combinations without tiring the palate.
How do I make the strawberry granita?

Puree the strawberries thoroughly, freeze in a shallow plastic container, and every fifteen minutes or so stir and rake with a fork to break up the ice crystals; in about two hours or less it's frozen. Scrape again before serving to restore the texture.
What strawberries should I use?
Exceptional ones. The author says not to bother with hard, tasteless berries that made a 2000-mile trip to your grocery store; the granita has just one ingredient: strawberries.
What replaces the graham cracker crust?
A salty one of coarsely pulverized rice crackers and mini pretzels with butter, fennel pollen and black pepper, processed to bits about 1/4 to 1/2 the size of a grain of puffed rice cereal.
How do I assemble it?

Oil a 1-inch ring mold on a plate, press in a 1/2-inch layer of crust, top with 3 tablespoons of chevre pressed into the mold, gently push out the "cheesecake," and top with a tablespoon of granita. Serve immediately.

summary: Ten-minute chickpea salad with feta and basil: two cans of chickpeas, red onion, cucumber, roasted peppers, 1/2 pound crumbled feta, garlic, basil, lemon juice and olive oil tossed together in 10 minutes; serves 3 as an entree, 8 as a side or 12 for a potluck.
glance: 3 as an entree, 8 as a side dish, or 12 for a potluck
serve right away or refrigerate up to a few hours
yield: 3 as an entree, 8 as a side dish, or 12 for a potluck
faq: How does the dressing form?
As you toss it, the crumbled feta dissolves a little and makes a creamy dressing.
Why keep a stocked pantry?

The recipe shows why it's good to keep cans of chickpeas, roasted peppers and good olive oil: when you don't have time to cook, you can still get something great on the table. It was invented at 5:30 for a 6:00 block party potluck.
Can I change the ingredients?

Add or substitute other herbs (tarragon, dill or mint), olives, blanched green beans or artichoke hearts. The author's wife adds a few cups of prepared Israeli couscous (large pearls, not the tiny grains of traditional couscous).
Do I need to add salt?
Taste first and add salt as needed. Depending on how salty your feta is, you might not need any.
How long does it keep?
Serve right away, or refrigerate for up to a few hours.

summary: Challah French toast bread pudding: cubed challah or brioche soaked in a vanilla-cinnamon custard overnight and baked at 375°F for about 45 minutes until golden and about 190°F inside; a do-ahead brunch dish for 4 that you can sweeten, spice or make savory.
glance: 4 eggs, 2 cups milk, vanilla, cinnamon, salt, 3 tablespoons sugar
375°F, about 45 minutes, until golden and about 190°F inside
faq: Why challah for French toast?

Challah (and its cousin brioche) makes the finest French toast imaginable: the bread is already eggy, so the custard takes it over the top. The author usually has most of a loaf left over after Friday night Shabbat.
What's the difference between French toast and bread pudding?
The author concluded there really isn't much of one, except that the bread is diced. Slice-and-bake French toast in a casserole is a great do-ahead item for a brunch with guests.
How much custard do I need?

Proportions are approximate, depending on how much bread you have and how stale it is. Pour the custard on a bit at a time and stop when the bread is quite wet throughout (the texture of French toast before cooking), or mix up a bit more if needed.
Do I need to remove the crust?
Challah is typically braided, so it's hard to remove all the crust without wasting too much; do the best you can, a little crust won't bother anyone.
How can I vary it?
Add roasted pears and brown sugar, or apples and maple syrup, or orange zest and triple sec; serve it with ice cream for dessert; or go savory with, say, manchego and smoked paprika.
Is the overnight rest necessary?
The author says it might not be all that necessary but he hasn't tried skipping it; it would probably be fine.

summary: Sauteed corn with lemongrass: fresh corn kernels stir-fried over very high heat for 2-3 minutes with lemongrass, ginger, garlic, kaffir lime leaf, chiles, squash and bell pepper, finished with lime zest and juice, tomatoes and green onions; vegan, serves 4 to 6 in 20 minutes.
glance: kernels from 5 ears of fresh sweet corn (not frozen)
1 minute aromatics, 1 minute squash and pepper, 2-3 minutes corn
faq: Why not use frozen corn?
This is one recipe where frozen won't do: used still frozen, it lowers the heat too much, and if you defrost first, the kernels will be soggy.
What flavors does corn pair with?
Corn has a great affinity for the Southeast Asian flavors of lemongrass, lime, ginger and chiles. Sauteeing it over high heat with all of these aromatics makes a bright, flavorful side dish.
How do I prepare lemongrass?

Remove all but the bottom 3 inches, keeping only the nearly white portion, trim 1/4 inch off the bottom end, remove the tough outer layers, then whack the piece several times with the bottom of a saucepan or the side of a cleaver until rather flattened, and mince.
What do I serve it with?
The author suggests the quinoa cakes for a perfect late-summer dinner.
How do I finish it?
Add the lime juice and turn off the heat, remove the kaffir lime leaves, adjust seasoning, and garnish with halved cherry tomatoes, green onions, black pepper and a few flakes of sea salt.

summary: Soba noodles in shiitake shoyu broth with spring vegetables: dried shiitake, kombu, ginger and garlic simmered 20 minutes with leeks added for 10 more, seasoned with shoyu and served over buckwheat noodles with 8-minute eggs, grilled asparagus, soft tofu and green onions; serves 4 in 45 minutes.
glance: 8 cups water, 2 cups dried shiitake and kombu, 20 minutes, leeks 10 more, 3 tablespoons shoyu
cold water to a boil, covered off the heat for exactly 8 minutes
faq: What are soba noodles?

Japanese noodles made from buckwheat flour, often served cold with a dipping sauce but equally great in hot soup. The buckwheat flavor is distinctively nutty and earthy, which reminds the author of the kasha his Eastern European Jewish family served.
How do I make an umami-rich vegetarian broth?

Rinse dried shiitakes and simmer them with kombu, ginger and garlic in 8 cups of water for 20 minutes, add the leeks for 10 more minutes, then strain through a fine sieve squeezing the mushrooms, and season with 3 tablespoons of shoyu.
What is shoyu?

The Japanese name for soy sauce. Unpasteurized nama shoyu is to most others as Parmigiano-Reggiano is to the stuff in the green can: more complex and caramelized, less salty, no chemical edge, and claimed to be a source of probiotic bacteria.
How do I cook the eggs?

Cover eggs with cold water by 1/2 inch, bring to a boil over high heat, cover and remove from the heat, then set a timer for exactly 8 minutes and shock in cold water. The whites and yolk are set but the yolk is slightly underdone, bright yellow and translucent.
Can I change the toppings?
Yes. These are a transition from winter (leeks, dried mushrooms) to spring (asparagus, eggs); vary to suit your mood and your vegetable drawer, or use ramen or udon noodles.

summary: Bunuelos (bimuelos), Sephardic Hanukkah donuts, with a review of Lara Ferroni's Doughnuts: a quite wet yeast dough risen at least an hour, shaped with wet hands into rustic holed rounds, deep fried at 370°F and served with honey or powdered sugar; makes about 14.
glance: 2 1/4 teaspoons yeast, 2 cups warm water, 3 1/4 cups flour; rise at least 1 hour (up to 4)
3 inches of oil at 370°F, golden on each side
Vegetarian; vegan with powdered sugar instead of honey
faq: What are bunuelos?

A rustic yeast-raised and fried donut made by the Sephardic side of the author's family, eaten at Hanukkah with traditional honey and any other time with powdered sugar. There is a Passover version made with matzoh, but the author says it doesn't hold a candle to the flour-based one.
How do I shape the dough?

The dough should be quite wet and isn't rolled out: wet your hands, grab about 3 tablespoons of dough, form a rough ball and poke a hole through the center with your thumb, then drop it carefully into the oil. They're meant to be rustic; don't try to make them perfect.
How long can the dough rise?
At least 1 hour in a warm spot. The author has let it go four hours, stirring it down occasionally, and says it only gets more delicious.
What is the Doughnuts cookbook?

Lara Ferroni's Doughnuts: Simple and Delicious Recipes to Make at Home, with fundamental recipes from classic raised to gluten-free cake doughnuts, specialty items like Hawaiian malasadas, and flavors from German chocolate to brandied eggnog; the author calls it approachable and beautifully photographed.
Can I make them on short notice?
Yes: you could stir up the dough in a few minutes before dinner and fry afterwards to entertain the kids.

summary: Tempeh and Japanese eggplant with crispy rice, a refrigerator cleanout supper: brown rice toasted in a covered pan into a crispy dome, thin tempeh slabs fried well browned, and lemongrass-garlic stir-fried eggplant, topped with green onion and cucumber; serves 4 as a one-dish supper.
glance: 3 cups cooked brown rice, toasted on low heat so a crispy layer forms on the bottom
8 ounces, 1/4-inch slabs fried in 1/8 inch of oil until browned
Vegetarian and vegan; potentially gluten-free if the tempeh is
faq: How do I make tempeh taste good?

Thoroughly fry it. Straight from the package it's cold soy-mush; the magic happens when it is pan fried in a single layer with enough oil that the outside really browns, becoming semi-crispy with a complex, nutty flavor. Maximize surface area by slicing it thinly.
How do I get the crispy rice?

Coat a small saucepan with 1 tablespoon of oil, fill it with the rice, cover and set on a low flame, adjusting so the rice toasts but doesn't burn, without disturbing the bottom layer. The longer you cook, the more toasted rice you get. Turn it out as a crispy dome, or just mound it.
What kind of eggplant?
Japanese eggplants, the long, thin kind, sliced into 1/2-inch half-moons, stir-fried with lemongrass and garlic.
Is this a recipe or a template?
The author calls it a refrigerator cleanout party and says you could adapt any part of it to your own needs; the cooked brown rice, tempeh, eggplant and lemongrass were simply what he found.
Why do people dislike tempeh?
One friend tweeted that it has the texture of an alien's brain; the author knew exactly what he meant, which is why it's essential to fry it thoroughly.

summary: Potato and green bean salad with arugula pesto: small waxy potatoes simmered from cold salted water until fork-tender, green beans boiled 2 1/2 minutes, both rinsed cold and tossed with a bright green arugula, olive oil, garlic and grana padano pesto; 15 minutes active, 1 hour total, serves 4.
glance: about 3 cups baby arugula, 3 tablespoons olive oil, garlic, grana padano; made close to serving time
faq: Why arugula pesto?
The pesto is a bright emerald green that holds its color much better than basil-based pesto, so the salad grabs attention on a buffet table.
When should I make the pesto?
As close to serving time as possible, because the fresh flavors begin to dissipate, emphasizing the bitter aspect of the arugula.
How do I cook the potatoes?

Start them in cold salted water (2 tablespoons of salt): that gives the interior a chance to cook before the outside has gone to mush. Bring to a boil, then keep a vigorous simmer until fork-tender, then cut larger ones in half.
How do I cook the green beans?
After removing the potatoes, boil the trimmed, halved beans in the same water for 2 1/2 minutes, then rinse both vegetables in cold water until cool.
What can I add?
Toasted walnut pieces and fresh ground black pepper. (A version of this pesto with mint is used in the author's cookbook.)

summary: Tomato jam with rosemary and saffron: 24 ounces of peeled diced tomatoes simmered about an hour with onion, sugar, rosemary, saffron, chili flakes and lemon juice until thick and syrupy; makes about 1 cup that keeps a few days refrigerated, good on grilled cheese.
glance: simmer about 1 hour, until thick and syrupy; no added liquid
a few days in the refrigerator
faq: What is tomato jam?

A piquant jam (or chutney) made by cooking tomatoes, a fruit after all, down with sugar and seasonings. The author loves it on a grilled cheese with seriously sharp cheddar, or with chickpea fritters.
Why peel the tomatoes?
Otherwise you'll have unpleasant stringy bits in the jam. Make an X in the skin at the end away from the stem, dunk in boiling water for 10 seconds, cool, and the skin zips right off.
Can I use imperfect tomatoes?
Yes, you don't need picture-perfect ones: ask at your farmer's market for seconds that are bruised or unloved, which the author says are about half the price of the number ones.
What other flavors work?
The jam uses rosemary, saffron and chili flakes, but garlic and lemon zest, or coriander, turmeric and black pepper, could be equally delicious.
Can I can it?
The author isn't a canner, so he doesn't know whether it's suitable for processing and longer-term storage; he says it keeps in the fridge for a few days.
